title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
seo_title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Multiply fractions by whole numbers and by fractions; divide fractions by whole numbers and by fractions; find a fraction of a quantity. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions: fraction of an amount, fraction × whole number, fraction × fraction, division of fractions and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: To divide, turn the second fraction upside down and multiply.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Fraction × fraction: multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 2/3 × 3/5 = 6/15 = 2/5.
  • Of means multiply: 3/4 of 20 = 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15.
  • To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal (turn it upside down): 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/4 × 2/1 = 1 1/2.

Examples

Example

2/5 × 15

15 ÷ 5 × 2

Answer: 6

Example

5/6 ÷ 2/3

5/6 × 3/2 = 15/12

Answer: 1 1/4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Turning the first fraction upside downOnly the fraction you divide by is turned over.
Multiplying the whole number by the denominator2/5 × 15 = 30/5 = 6, not 2/75.
Expecting multiplying to make biggerMultiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a number smaller.

faq.a: A fraction turned upside down: the reciprocal of 2/3 is 3/2.

faq.q: Why does dividing by 1/2 double a number?
faq.a: There are two halves in every whole.
Yes. It makes the numbers smaller.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 25 shaded in each. What is 3 × 25?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 2 is 3 × 2 = 6. Each part is 15, so 3 × 25 = 65, which is 1 15. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 5.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 4 bars with 13 shaded in each. What is 4 × 13?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 lots of 1 is 4 × 1 = 4. Each part is 13, so 4 × 13 = 43, which is 1 13. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 3.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 5 bars with 14 shaded in each. What is 5 × 14?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 5 lots of 1 is 5 × 1 = 5. Each part is 14, so 5 × 14 = 54, which is 1 14. The parts are still quarters, so the denominator stays 4.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 47 shaded in each. What is 3 × 47?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12. Each part is 17, so 3 × 47 = 127, which is 1 57. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 7.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 38 shaded in each. What is 3 × 38?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 3 is 3 × 3 = 9. Each part is 18, so 3 × 38 = 98, which is 1 18. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 8.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 4 bars with 25 shaded in each. What is 4 × 25?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 lots of 2 is 4 × 2 = 8. Each part is 15, so 4 × 25 = 85, which is 1 35. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 5.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 38?
c: 48 + 38
38 + 38 + 38
38 + 38 + 38 + 38
items.e: 4 × 38 means 4 lots of 38, so add 38 4 times: 38 + 38 + 38 + 38 = 128.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 3 × 29?
c: 39 + 29
29 + 29
29 + 29 + 29
items.e: 3 × 29 means 3 lots of 29, so add 29 3 times: 29 + 29 + 29 = 69.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 5 × 23?
c: 23 + 23 + 23 + 23
53 + 23
23 + 23 + 23 + 23 + 23
items.e: 5 × 23 means 5 lots of 23, so add 23 5 times: 23 + 23 + 23 + 23 + 23 = 103.

items.q: 29 + 29 + 29 + 29 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all ninths: 29 + 29 + 29 + 29 = 89. This is the same as 4 × 29. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all eighths: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = 58. This is the same as 5 × 18. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 310 + 310 + 310 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all tenths: 310 + 310 + 310 = 910. This is the same as 3 × 310. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 3 × 27 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 2 = 6, so the answer is 67.

items.q: 15 × 4 = ?
items.e: 15 × 4 is the same as 4 × 15. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 1 = 4, so the answer is 45.

items.q: 2 × 49 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 2 × 4 = 8, so the answer is 89.

items.q: 110 × 7 = ?
items.e: 110 × 7 is the same as 7 × 110. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 1 = 7, so the answer is 710.

items.q: 5 × 15 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 5 × 1 = 5, so the answer is 55. 5 ÷ 5 = 1, so the answer is 1.

items.q: 23 × 3 = ?
items.e: 23 × 3 is the same as 3 × 23. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 2 = 6, so the answer is 63. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so the answer is 2.

items.q: 4 × 34 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 3 = 12, so the answer is 124. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the answer is 3.

items.q: 311 × 3 = ?
items.e: 311 × 3 is the same as 3 × 311. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 3 = 9, so the answer is 911.

items.q: The whole bar is 12. Find 23 of 12.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 of 12 = 8.

items.q: The whole bar is 20. 34 × 20 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 5 = 15. So 34 of 20 = 15.

items.q: The whole bar is 25. 25 × 35 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 5 = 15. So 35 of 25 = 15.

items.q: The whole bar is 24. 56 × 24 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 4 = 20. So 56 of 24 = 20.

items.q: The whole bar is 36. Find 49 of 36.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 4 × 4 = 16. So 49 of 36 = 16.

items.q: Find 38 of 32.

items.q: 34 × 28 = ?

items.q: 40 × 35 = ?

items.q: Find 27 of 35.

items.q: 56 × 42 = ?

items.q: The whole bar is 20. What is 35 × 20?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 of 20 = 12. (Do not multiply the denominator by 20 as well: 60100 is just 35.)

items.q: The whole bar is 24. What is 34 × 24?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 6 = 18. So 34 of 24 = 18.

items.q: The whole bar is 18. What is 23 × 18?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 6 = 12. So 23 of 18 = 12.

items.q: The whole bar is 40. What is 58 × 40?

items.e: Divide by the denominator: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 4 × 4 = 16. So 47 of 28 = 16.

items.q: 38 × 24 = ?

items.q: 36 × 34 = ?

items.q: Find 56 of 30.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 5 = 25. So 56 of 30 = 25.

items.q: 710 × 50 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 7 × 5 = 35. So 710 of 50 = 35.

items.q: Find 29 of 45.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 5 = 10. So 29 of 45 = 10.

items.q: 14 × 12 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 4 × 2 = 8. So 14 × 12 = 18. This is already in its simplest form: 18. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 13 × 15 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 3 × 5 = 15. So 13 × 15 = 115. This is already in its simplest form: 115. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 12 × 16 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 2 × 6 = 12. So 12 × 16 = 112. This is already in its simplest form: 112. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 15 × 14 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. So 15 × 14 = 120. This is already in its simplest form: 120. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 13 × 13 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 3 × 3 = 9. So 13 × 13 = 19. This is already in its simplest form: 19. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 17 × 12 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. Multiply the denominators: 7 × 2 = 14. So 17 × 12 = 114. This is already in its simplest form: 114. The answer is smaller than both fractions, because you are finding a part of a part.

items.q: 23 × 45 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 2 × 4 = 8. Multiply the denominators: 3 × 5 = 15. So 23 × 45 = 815. This is already in its simplest form: 815. You do not need a common denominator to multiply.

items.q: 34 × 15 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 3 × 1 = 3. Multiply the denominators: 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 × 15 = 320. This is already in its simplest form: 320. You do not need a common denominator to multiply.

items.q: 49 × 23 = ?

items.q: 58 × 34 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 5 × 3 = 15. Multiply the denominators: 8 × 4 = 32. So 58 × 34 = 1532. This is already in its simplest form: 1532. You do not need a common denominator to multiply.

items.q:
23 × 34 = ?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 2 × 3 = 6. Multiply the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. So 23 × 34 = 612. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator by 6: 612 = 12.

items.q:

Give your answer in its simplest form.

Give your answer in its simplest form.

items.q: 12 × ? = 110
items.e: The numerators: 1 × 1 = 1. The denominators: 2 × ? = 10, so the missing denominator is 5. 12 × 15 = 110, so the missing fraction is 15.

items.q: ? × 23 = 29
items.e: The numerators: 1 × 2 = 2. The denominators: 3 × 3 = 9. 13 × 23 = 29, so the missing fraction is 13.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 13. It is split into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
13 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 3 × 2 = 6 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 13 ÷ 2 = 16. Check: 16 × 2 = 26 = 13.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 12. It is split into 4 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
12 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 2 × 4 = 8 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14. Multiply the denominator by 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 48 = 12.

items.q:

14 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 4 × 2 = 8 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 14 ÷ 2 = 18. Check: 18 × 2 = 28 = 14.

13 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 3 × 3 = 9 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by 13. Multiply the denominator by 3: 13 ÷ 3 = 19. Check: 19 × 3 = 39 = 13.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 15. It is split into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
15 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 15 ÷ 2 = 110. Check: 110 × 2 = 210 = 15.

12 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: Follow the dashed lines: the whole bar is cut into 2 × 3 = 6 equal parts, and the dark part is 1 of them. Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by 13. Multiply the denominator by 3: 12 ÷ 3 = 16. Check: 16 × 3 = 36 = 12.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 45. It is split into 2 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
45 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: The whole bar is cut into 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts, and 4 of them are dark: 410 = 25. The numerator 4 can be divided by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Keep the denominator: 45 ÷ 2 = 25. Check: 25 × 2 = 45.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 23. It is split into 4 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
23 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: The whole bar is cut into 3 × 4 = 12 equal parts, and 2 of them are dark: 212 = 16. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14. Multiply the denominator by 4: 23 ÷ 4 = 212. Simplify: 212 = 16. Check: 16 × 4 = 46 = 23.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 34. It is split into 3 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
34 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: The whole bar is cut into 4 × 3 = 12 equal parts, and 3 of them are dark: 312 = 14. The numerator 3 can be divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Keep the denominator: 34 ÷ 3 = 14. Check: 14 × 3 = 34.

items.q:
The bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 67. It is split into 3 equal parts. What fraction of the whole bar is the dark part?
67 ÷ 3 = ?
items.e: The whole bar is cut into 7 × 3 = 21 equal parts, and 6 of them are dark: 621 = 27. The numerator 6 can be divided by 3: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Keep the denominator: 67 ÷ 3 = 27. Check: 27 × 3 = 67.

items.q: 5 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 6 sixths. 5 wholes have 5 × 6 = 30 sixths, so 5 ÷ 16 = 30. Check: 30 × 16 = 306 = 5.

items.q: 6 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 4 fourths. 6 wholes have 6 × 4 = 24 fourths, so 6 ÷ 14 = 24. Check: 24 × 14 = 244 = 6.

items.q: 7 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 3 thirds. 7 wholes have 7 × 3 = 21 thirds, so 7 ÷ 13 = 21. Check: 21 × 13 = 213 = 7.

items.q: 10 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: Each whole has 2 halves. 10 wholes have 10 × 2 = 20 halves, so 10 ÷ 12 = 20. Check: 20 × 12 = 202 = 10.

items.q: 17 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Cut 17 into 2 equal parts. Then 1 whole has 7 × 2 = 14 of these parts, so each part is 114. 17 ÷ 2 = 114. Check: 114 × 2 = 214 = 17.

items.q: 14 ÷ 5 = ?
items.e: Cut 14 into 5 equal parts. Then 1 whole has 4 × 5 = 20 of these parts, so each part is 120. 14 ÷ 5 = 120. Check: 120 × 5 = 520 = 14.

items.q: 19 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Cut 19 into 2 equal parts. Then 1 whole has 9 × 2 = 18 of these parts, so each part is 118. 19 ÷ 2 = 118. Check: 118 × 2 = 218 = 19.

items.q: 16 ÷ 4 = ?
items.e: Cut 16 into 4 equal parts. Then 1 whole has 6 × 4 = 24 of these parts, so each part is 124. 16 ÷ 4 = 124. Check: 124 × 4 = 424 = 16.

items.q: To check 4 ÷ 13 = 12, which multiplication should you do?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by. It should give the number you started with: 12 × 13 = 123 = 4. It matches, so 12 is right.

items.q: To check 2 ÷ 18 = 16, which multiplication should you do?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by. It should give the number you started with: 16 × 18 = 168 = 2. It matches, so 16 is right.

items.q: Each bottle holds 34 of a litre of water. How much water is in 6 bottles?
items.e: 6 × 34. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 184. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, so 184 = 4 24 = 4 12 litres.

items.q: A loaf of bread needs 25 kg of flour. How much flour is needed for 4 loaves?
items.e: 4 × 25. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is 85. 8 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 3, so 85 = 1 35 kg.

items.q: Each bow uses 35 m of ribbon. Halima makes 7 bows. How much ribbon does she use?
items.e: 7 × 35. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 3 = 21, so the answer is 215. 21 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 1, so 215 = 4 15 m.

items.q: Each lesson lasts 34 of an hour. How many hours are 5 lessons?
items.e: 5 × 34. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 5 × 3 = 15, so the answer is 154. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 3, so 154 = 3 34 hours.

items.q: Each pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Each of 6 pupils eats 38 of a pizza. How much pizza do they eat altogether?
items.e: 6 × 38. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 188. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 2, so 188 = 2 28 = 2 14 pizzas.

items.q: Fatima reads for 23 of an hour every night. How many hours does she read in 7 nights?
items.e: 7 × 23. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 2 = 14, so the answer is 143. 14 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 2, so 143 = 4 23 hours.

items.q: There are 32 pupils in a Primary 5 class. 38 of them have school lunch. How many pupils have school lunch?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 4 = 12. So 38 of 32 = 12 pupils.

items.q: A football match lasts 90 minutes. 23 of the match has been played. How many minutes is that?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 30 = 60. So 23 of 90 = 60 minutes.

items.q: A box has 45 packets of crisps. 25 of the packets are cheese and onion. How many packets are cheese and onion?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 9 = 18. So 25 of 45 = 18 packets.

items.q: A bag of potatoes weighs 2 12 kg. The school cook buys 3 bags. How much do they weigh altogether?
items.e: Partition 2 12 into 2 and 12. Multiply each part by 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 12 × 3 = 32 = 1 12. Add: 6 + 1 12 = 7 12 kg.

items.q: 34 × 16 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 3 × 1 = 3. Multiply the denominators: 4 × 6 = 24. So 34 × 16 = 324. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator by 3: 324 = 18.

items.q: 56 ÷ 5 = ?
items.e: The numerator 5 can be divided by 5: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Keep the denominator: 56 ÷ 5 = 16. Check: 16 × 5 = 56.

items.q: 25 × 35 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 7 = 14. So 25 of 35 = 14.

items.q: 78 ÷ 2 = ?
items.e: Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 12. Multiply the denominator by 2: 78 ÷ 2 = 716. Check: 716 × 2 = 1416 = 78.

items.q: 49 × 38 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerators: 4 × 3 = 12. Multiply the denominators: 9 × 8 = 72. So 49 × 38 = 1272. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator by 12: 1272 = 16.

items.q: 34 of a pizza is left. Chidi eats half of what is left. What fraction of the whole pizza does he eat?
items.e: Half of 34 means 12 × 34. Multiply the numerators: 1 × 3 = 3. Multiply the denominators: 2 × 4 = 8. So 12 × 34 = 38. This is already in its simplest form: 38. He eats 38 of the pizza.

items.q: 23 of a cake is left. Uche shares it equally between 4 friends. What fraction of the whole cake does each friend get?
items.e: Share 23 between 4: 23 ÷ 4. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by 14. Multiply the denominator by 4: 23 ÷ 4 = 212. Simplify: 212 = 16. Check: 16 × 4 = 46 = 23.

items.q: A bottle holds 34 of a litre of juice. It is poured equally into 3 glasses. How much juice is in each glass?
items.e: 34 ÷ 3: The numerator 3 can be divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Keep the denominator: 34 ÷ 3 = 14 litre. Check: 14 × 3 = 34.

items.q: Ifeoma has a ribbon 25 m long. She cuts it into 2 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 25 ÷ 2: The numerator 2 can be divided by 2: 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Keep the denominator: 25 ÷ 2 = 15 m. Check: 15 × 2 = 25.

items.q: There are 30 pupils in a Primary 6 class. 35 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 6 = 18. So 35 of 30 = 18.
